If you have ever struggled to make your house truly feel like a home, you are not alone. That is why every seasonal chapter in Homemaking with Babs includes ideas for adding the comforting, personal touches that make a home feel like yours.

While we were in Charleston, we posted on Stories asking if anyone would let me come over and help organize their home.

Lauren invited us in.

We thought the day would be about sharing a few organizing tips, but what it became was so much more.

Lauren already had a beautiful, organized house. But since losing her mom two years ago shortly after she started building her house, she had been struggling to now make it truly feel like home. She missed having her mom there to say, “Okay, here is what you do.”

So we spent the day making small, comforting changes using ideas from my new book.

We brought her mother’s vase and silver out of storage. We displayed her children’s artwork, created a craft and homework cart for calmer afternoons, and framed old photographs of her mom so Lauren could see her every time she walked through the door.

Nothing we did completely changed her house. But each little detail made it feel warmer, more personal and more connected to the people she loves.

Because homemaking is not about having a perfect house or buying more things. It is about bringing the meaningful things you already have into your everyday life and creating a home where the people inside feel seen, loved and cared for.

Lauren later told me there were so many things she did not know she still needed her mom to teach her.

That is why I wrote Homemaking with Babs. So whenever you need a little motherly guidance, you can open the book and hear me say, “Okay, here is what you do.” ❤️

Click the link in my bio for the recipes! We celebrated Labor Day a little early this year because I was about to hit the road for the Homemaking with Babs book tour, and I couldn’t leave without squeezing in one last summer dinner at the beach. ❤️

And what a way to send off summer!

I did as much of the prep as I could at home, packed it all up, and finished dinner right at the beach. If your beach or park has grills available, take advantage of them! It’s such a fun way to turn an ordinary summer evening into something that feels really special. Just be sure to check your beach’s rules before you plan your menu.

Now that I’m home from the first stops of the book tour, I’m finally getting to share everything we made.

And what a menu it was!

Click the link in my bio to get your copy of Homemaking with Babs!

The very first event of the Homemaking with Babs book tour felt especially meaningful because we held it right here at the Basket House. For the first time ever, we opened the doors and welcomed 60 of my online family inside to tour the home, hear some of its stories, and celebrate the book together.

The Basket House is where so much of Homemaking with Babs was photographed, so beginning the tour here felt like the perfect way to bring everything full circle.

And it reminded me of something I really wanted this book to capture: homemaking is about so much more than cleaning and organizing.
Yes, it is about creating systems that make life easier, staying on top of home maintenance, building routines that work, and having seasonal checklists and practical tips to help you care for your home.
But it is also about what happens inside that home.

It is about gathering around the table, welcoming people in, feeding the people you love, celebrating together, and making your home a place people want to return to.

That is why Homemaking with Babs also includes so much of what I have learned over a lifetime of hosting and entertaining, from how to set a table and the entertaining essentials I always keep on hand, to simple ways to spruce up for the season and even my trick for nearly doubling the size of your table when you need a few more seats.

Because your home is meant to be cared for, but it is also meant to be lived in, gathered in, and shared.

What a special way to begin this book tour and thank you @Birch Lane for making this such a special day!

We aren’t born knowing how to run a home, and they certainly don’t teach us in school.

After more than 50 years of homemaking, I wanted to put everything I’ve learned in one place. The things your mother taught you, the things she may have forgotten to teach you, and the things you usually only learn after years of figuring them out yourself.

Homemaking with Babs is filled with my tried-and-true DIY cleaners, cleaning routines, seasonal schedules, home maintenance checklists, organizing systems, and all those little tips that make taking care of a home so much easier.

Whether you’re moving into your very first home or you’ve been taking care of one for decades, I hope this is the book you keep nearby, turn to when you need it, and eventually pass along to someone you love.

It’s the owner’s manual your home should have come with. 🤍

Homemaking with Babs arrives September 1!

What if just 15 minutes in the morning and 15 minutes at night could change more than your home?

The Babs Method is just one of the practical, life-changing systems inside Homemaking with Babs. I poured a lifetime of knowledge into this book to help your home run more smoothly—and help you feel calmer and more in control.

When everything around you is piling up, your mind carries the weight of every unfinished task. You can feel behind before the day has even begun.

But a few simple routines can change that. Your home stays manageable, your mind feels clearer, and you stop using so much energy worrying about everything you still need to do.

It isn’t about having a perfect home. It’s about creating simple systems that give you more peace, more energy, and more time for the life happening inside it.

When your home feels lighter, your mind does too. 🤍

Click the link in my bio to get my new book, Homemaking with Babs! Everything I've learned about caring for a home, all in one place. 

I've spent a lifetime figuring out the little things that make caring for a home easier and I decided it was time to put everything I've learned in one place.

Because nobody teaches us how to run a home. Most of us learn as we go... one spill, stain, mess, and "How on earth do I fix THAT?" at a time. That's why I wrote Homemaking with Babs. 

Inside, I'm sharing:
cleaning tricks
DIY solutions
organizing systems
seasonal to-do lists
routines
home-maintenance 

All the know-hows l've gathered over the years—all organized to help you care for your home through every season.

My hope is that whenever something comes up and you think, "Babs, what do I do?" you can pull this book off the shelf find the answer. This is the book I hope you dog-ear, write in, spill coffee on, and reach for again and again.

Click the link in my bio to order my new book Homemaking with Babs!

Inside, you’ll find the systems I’ve used for a lifetime. From The Babs Method (just 15 minutes every morning and every evening) to simple daily, weekly, and monthly routines that help you stay ahead instead of constantly catching up.

Then we’ll walk through the year together. Season by season.

🍂 Fall routines and family organization
❄️ Winter homemaking, hosting, and home care.
🌸 Spring cleaning and decluttering
☀️ Summer outdoor living

Plus seasonal checklists, organizing systems, DIY cleaners, home maintenance, and practical tips to help every room-and every season-feel a little easier.

My hope is that this becomes the book you pull off the shelf again and again whenever you need a little guidance, a little encouragement, or simply a better system.

Because here’s what I’ve learned: you don’t need a perfectly organized home-you need simple systems that work for YOUR family.

Today we reset the fridge and freezer, used my homemade all purpose cleaner, created dinner bins, stocked a few make-ahead meals, made a 2 a.m.-ready stomach bug bucket, used my five-bin system to declutter, created homework and family drop zones-and most importantly, got the kids involved so keeping the home running doesn’t fall on one person.

And this is exactly what the Fall chapter of Homemaking with Babs is all about 🍂

The entire book follows the rhythm of the seasons, helping you know what to tackle, when to tackle it, and how to create routines that make caring for your home feel a whole lot less overwhelming.

Because homemaking isn’t about perfection. It’s about creating a home that works for the people who live in it ❤️
